app.name: HOTAS Mapper
step.label: Steps
error.not-dcs-folder: That folder is not a DCS settings folder. Pick Saved Games\DCS or Saved Games\DCS\Config\Input.
aircraft.title: Which aircraft are you setting up?
aircraft.lead: Every module has its own list of commands. You will map them onto your stick, throttle and pedals in step 3.
aircraft.missing: Don't see your aircraft? Command lists are added module by module.
devices.title: What do you fly with?
devices.lead: Add each device you use. You will see it as a picture with every real button and hat, so you never have to guess what “button 14” is.
devices.libraryMissing: Your device is not here yet? Devices are added to the library one by one.
devices.emptySetup: Add a device from the library.
devices.folder.title: Connect your DCS settings folder
devices.folder.why: DCS names each device with an ID unique to your PC. Open Saved Games\DCS, usually %USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\DCS, so the right IDs and your current bindings can be used.
devices.folder.private: Read only: files are read in your browser — nothing is uploaded and nothing on your PC is changed.
devices.folder.found: Found {devices} devices and bindings for {aircraft} aircraft.
devices.id.matched: Matched with your DCS folder ({count} found).
devices.id.typed: Not found in your DCS folder. Check that it matches the name on the DCS Controls screen.
devices.id.missing: Pick or paste the full name from the DCS Controls screen, including the {…} part. Without it the file cannot be written.
devices.start.noPreset: {aircraft} has no ED preset for this device
devices.start.noCurrent: Connect your DCS folder and pick the device ID
devices.start.fileHint: Your own or shared by someone else (.diff.lua)
map.how1: Click the field next to an action
map.how2: Press the button on your device
map.how3: Or press any button first to see what it does.
map.carryText: Press the new button on your device, or click it on the picture. The modifier and the tune go with it.
map.carryTextAxis: Move the new axis on your device, or click it on the picture. The modifier and the tune go with it.
map.nothingYet: Nothing yet — this button is free
map.uiUses: UI Layer: {name} — works in every aircraft
map.howToPut: To put a command here: click its field in the table, then press this button.
map.pictureHint: Hover a number to see its command. Numbering as in the maker’s software.
map.drawerLook: Click a number to see what it does
map.footer: {count} bindings on the shown devices · {problems} won’t work
problem.dead: DCS ignores this command until you save it again
problem.modifierKey: This button is a modifier on this device
problem.uiLayer: Same button as “{name}” in UI Layer, so DCS ignores it here
problem.modifierUi: The button of modifier {name} is in UI Layer
export.title: Check and save
export.noId: No DCS device ID — this device will be skipped
export.skipped: {count} device(s) have no DCS ID and will be skipped.
map.openHint: Open one or more categories on the left.
map.notForJoystick: DCS offers this command only for the keyboard or mouse
link.title: Connect to this page
link.explainTitle: How the page sees your stick and throttle
link.explain: Your browser can read game controllers plugged into this computer (the Gamepad API built into Chrome, Edge and Firefox). Nothing to install and nothing leaves your PC. Link each device below by pressing a button on it; without linking you can still click the buttons on the device picture.
link.how: Click “Link”, then press any button on the {name}.
link.waiting: Waiting — press any button on the {name}. Press again if nothing happens.
link.unsupported: This browser cannot read game controllers. Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
map.pressToSee: press a button to see what it does
load.title: Already set up your controls in DCS?
load.text: Open your Saved Games\DCS folder. It is usually %USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\DCS: paste that into the address bar of the folder window and press Enter. Aircraft you have bindings for get marked; pick one and its devices and bindings load so you can see and change them.
load.connected: DCS folder connected — your bindings for {count} aircraft found.
load.pick: Pick a marked aircraft to load its devices and bindings.
load.badFile: {file} is not a DCS controls file.
devices.fromFileHint: A .diff.lua from Saved Games\DCS\Config\Input\<aircraft>\joystick — yours or someone else’s. You can pick several.
map.noPicture: No picture for this device yet. Numbers are the DCS button numbers: click a field and press the button on the device.
export.install2: Unzip the archive into Saved Games\DCS and let it replace the files there (copy them first if you want to go back).
export.install3: Start DCS and open Options › Controls › {aircraft} to check.
devices.pictureHint: Several devices can show up in DCS as “{name}” — e.g. a MOZA throttle plugged into the AB9 base. Picked by the buttons and axes your DCS files use; change it if it is wrong.
devices.pictureUnknown: Several devices can show up in DCS as “{name}”, and your DCS files do not tell which one this is. Choose it to see its picture.
export.comparedInstalled: Changes are compared with the files in your DCS folder now.
export.comparedDefaults: Your DCS folder is not open, so changes are compared with the DCS defaults. Open it on the first step to compare with what you have now.
devices.folder.offSummary: {count} turned off in DCS — listed below the active ones.
devices.turnOffHint: DCS then ignores this device in every aircraft.
devices.off.title: Turned off in DCS · {count}
devices.off.lead: DCS ignores these devices in every aircraft, so their bindings do nothing. It is the “Disabled” tick of a device in the DCS controls screen.
devices.off.noBindings: No bindings in your DCS folder
devices.off.saved: Saved in the download as Config\Input\disabled.lua, for all aircraft at once — as in DCS.
ff.hint: Force feedback of this device in this aircraft
ff.none: {aircraft} has no force feedback settings for this device
ff.lead: How hard the base pushes back in this aircraft. Other aircraft keep their own settings.
ff.trimmerHint: How strongly the base holds the stick where it is trimmed.
ff.shakeHint: How strong the vibration effects are: guns, buffeting, stall.
ff.swapAxesHint: Swap the left-right and forward-back forces
fix.freeUi: Remove it from UI Layer (all aircraft)
map.modsForBinding: Modifiers for this binding — hold one on your device, or pick:
mods.title: Modifiers and switches
mods.lead: In DCS a binding is one button plus any number of modifiers. A modifier is a button you hold, like Shift on a keyboard. A switch works the same, but one press turns it on and the next press turns it off. A button becomes a modifier only after you add it here.
mods.modifiersHint: Hold it, then press another button.
mods.switchesHint: Press once to turn it on, again to turn it off.
mods.noModifiers: No modifiers on your devices yet.
mods.name: Name
mods.press: Press the button you want to use
mods.pressHint: On the linked device of this tab. Or pick it below.
mods.uses: Used in {count} bindings — they stop working if you remove it
mods.busy: {input} already has a command: {command}. Once it is a modifier, DCS ignores commands on this button alone.
mods.uiBusy: {input} is “{name}” in UI Layer. DCS ignores bindings that use a modifier on this button.
mods.twin: This button is already the modifier “{name}”.
mods.nameTaken: A modifier with this name already exists.
mods.saved: Saved with your other files in Config\Input\{folder}\modifiers.lua.
tune.axes: This command has several axes on this device, each with its own settings:
tune.chart: Response curve: your axis across, what DCS gets up
tune.try: Move your stick to see where it lands on the curve, or drag here.
tune.pointsHint: Output at each tenth of the travel. DCS draws a smooth curve through these points.
tune.exact: Computed the way DCS computes it, so the curve here is the curve in the game.
why.title: {command} won’t work
why.dead: An aircraft update gave this command a default button that you already use for another command. DCS marks it as a conflict and ignores it until you change or clear it.
why.modifierKey: {input} is the modifier “{name}”. DCS uses a modifier button only to change what other buttons do, so a command on {input} itself never fires.
why.uiLayer: {input} is “{name}” in UI Layer, which works in every aircraft. DCS marks a command of this aircraft on the same button as a conflict and ignores it.
why.unknownModifier: {combo} needs the modifier “{name}”, but this aircraft has no modifier with that name. DCS skips bindings with modifiers it does not know.
why.modifierUi: The button of the modifier “{name}” is “{ui}” in UI Layer, so DCS ignores bindings that use this modifier.
map.uiNeedsModifier: A command of this aircraft on {input} needs a modifier, e.g. {example}. Without one, DCS treats it as a conflict with UI Layer.
export.sheetsLead: One picture per device with every binding of this aircraft written next to its button. PNG, A4 landscape — print it or keep it on a second screen.
export.noSheet: There is no picture of this device
sheet.numbers: Button numbers as in the maker’s software
editor.title: Device editor
editor.changes: {count} unsaved changes — download the folder to keep them
editor.name: Name
editor.namePlaceholder: e.g. MOZA AB9 FFB Base + MH16 grip
editor.dcsPlaceholder: Filled in when you press a button on the device
editor.dcsHint: As on the DCS Controls screen, without the {…} part — that is how the ED presets find it.
editor.pictureHint: PNG, JPG, WebP or SVG, up to 3 MB. A line drawing on a white background reads best. Use only pictures you made or may share.
editor.heading.buttons: Put the numbers on the picture
editor.heading.card: Card: the part shown in the device library
editor.drop: Drop a picture of the device here
editor.dropHint: A line drawing or a photo on a white background. Several pictures — say, two sides of a grip — are fine: add them one by one.
editor.bar.first: Add a picture first. Then press a button on your device and click where it is.
editor.bar.move: {input} selected — drag it, or click where it is on the picture. Press another button on your device to switch.
editor.bar.place: {input} — click where it is on the picture. The next one is picked for you.
editor.bar.done: All buttons are on the picture. Press one on your device to move it.
editor.bar.pick: Press a button, move a hat or an axis on your device — or pick it in the list.
editor.frameHint: Drag the frame to move it, its corner to resize it. Everything outside the frame stays hidden.
editor.layers: This view is put together from {count} pictures. Their places are set in device.json for now.
editor.buttonsCount: {placed} of {total} placed — press one on your device or pick it here
editor.cardHint: What people see on the device card when they pick their devices.
editor.viewHint: What the mapper shows next to the commands.
editor.sendHint: On GitHub open devices/{folder} → Add file → Upload files and drop the folder in. Or attach the .zip to an “Add a device” issue.
editor.tryFailed: This device is too big to try here — download the folder instead.
editor.needs: Give the device a name and at least one picture first.
map.moveAxisNow: Move an axis on your device — a button won’t do here. Or click an axis on the picture; the buttons are greyed out.
map.replaceAxisHint: The axis you move takes the place of {input}.
map.addAxisHint: Both axes will drive this command, each with its own Tune. DCS follows whichever moved last, e.g. two separate pedals on one rudder axis.
map.pressButtonNow: Press a button on your device. Or click its number on the picture; the axes are greyed out. Hold a modifier first for a second layer.
map.drawerAxis: Move an axis or click it to give it to {name}
map.drawerButton: Press a button or click its number to give it to {name}
map.needsAxis: {command} needs an axis — {input} is a button
map.needsButton: {command} needs a button — {input} is an axis
devices.pickHint: Click a device to add it to your setup, and click it again to take it out. If your setup has it more than once, take out the one you don't need with ×.
map.notOfferedHint: DCS does not offer this command for the {device}
devices.builtIn.keyboard: Press keys right in the table; Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win are already modifiers.
devices.builtIn.mouse: Five buttons, the wheel and movement. Pick them on the picture.
devices.builtIn.noLink.keyboard: Nothing to link: the page hears your keys
devices.builtIn.noLink.mouse: Nothing to link: pick the button on the picture
devices.start.dcsDefaults: No file yet — starts from the DCS defaults
devices.start.emptyBuiltIn: Removes the DCS default bindings too
map.pressKeyNow: Press the key. Hold Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win with it for a modifier. Or click the key on the picture.
map.pickMouseNow: Click the mouse button, the wheel or a movement on the picture.
map.pictureHint.keyboard: Every key of a full-size keyboard: the browser cannot tell which keys yours has. Hover a key to see its commands.
map.pictureHint.mouse: L, R — left and right button, M — wheel click, Z — wheel, X and Y — moving the mouse, 4 and 5 — side buttons. The browser cannot tell which buttons your mouse has.
editor.wholeHint: {count} pictures put together; numbers move on any of them
zoom.hint: Scroll the mouse wheel over the picture to zoom in, drag it to move.
editor.changesMany: {count} unsaved changes on {devices} devices — the download takes them all
